newsitem.title: USA: Civilian pilot reports close encounter with F-16s.
newsitem.headline: Civilian pilot reports close encounter with F-16s.

text.p: An American Eagle pilot reported that four F-16 military planes were flying "too close" to his aircraft over eastern Maryland on Friday, an FAA spokeswoman said, in the second incident involving civilian and military planes this week.

She said the plane, flying from Raleigh, North Carolina to JFK International airport in New York, continued on its regular course. The pilot told air traffic controllers in Leesburg, Virginia, he would file a "near mid-air collision" report, but he had not yet done so, she said.
"He said they were flying too close," spokeswoman Diane Stitaliere told Reuters. She said the passenger flight was flying at about 19,000 feet (5,791 metres) when the incident occured.
Paul Schlamm, a spokesman for the National Transportation and Safety Board, said: "We are investigating. The incident was reported by the pilot, who said the jets passed close enough to report it."

The NTSB said earlier Friday it would investigate an incident off the New Jersey coast on Wednesday involving a jetliner and two national guard F-16 jet fighters that the charter jet's operator described as a near collision.
In that incident the Boeing 727 with about 80 passengers maneuvered violently in response to electronic cockpit warnings when it was approached by one F-16.
